title: Module variables referenced by functions are marked unused
reasoning: Module scans skip function and class definitions entirely, dropping references to module bindings from those scopes. A module constant used by a function is therefore reported as unused. The same omission can classify a variable as single-use even when functions reference it repeatedly.
reproduction:
Analyze `LIMIT = 10
def limit():
    return LIMIT
`. The module scan records one definition and zero uses of LIMIT and emits an UnusedVariable.
recommendation: Resolve references across lexical scopes: count references to module bindings inside functions and classes while excluding locally shadowed names. Share this accounting between unused and single-use detection.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The supplied test covers dictionary merging and has no variable-use or lexical-scope assertions.
suggestedRegressionTest: Cover globals referenced from functions and methods, multiple references, local shadowing, and truly unused module bindings.
minimumFixScope: Module binding and reference accounting in waste.py.
